tagline: Connecting for good while transforming our business.
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the main driver of BT's strategic transformation: the ramp-up of the full fibre network is at the core of its future value, with leverage effects on quality, reliability, and residential and enterprise revenues. Over 50% of UK households and businesses now have access to faster and more reliable broadband.

kpis.name: Fibre coverage (premises)
kpis.explanation: Number of buildings connected or eligible for Openreach's ultra-fast full fibre network.
kpis.description: Openreach is expanding its full fibre network at a sustained pace, enabling over half of UK households and businesses to access faster and more reliable broadband.
kpis.signal: Over 50% of UK households and businesses now have access to full fibre thanks to Openreach's investments.

kpis.name: 5G population coverage
kpis.explanation: Percentage of the UK population covered by BT/EE's 5G network.
kpis.description: 5G coverage reaches 75% at the national level, with peaks at 77% in England and only 29% in Northern Ireland.
kpis.signal: Rapid 5G network expansion, despite marked regional disparities.

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.explanation: BT's consolidated turnover for the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Revenue declined to £20.4 billion (FY25), compared to £20.8 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Revenue decline of 2% in FY25, reflecting competitive and market pressures.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted gross operating result, excluding exceptional items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA improved to £8.2 billion (FY25), compared to £8.1 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Slight improvement in operating profitability (+1%) despite revenue decline.

kpis.name: Capital expenditure
kpis.description: Capital expenditure remained stable at £4.9 billion in FY25, identical to FY24. BT is the largest infrastructure investor in the FTSE 100, with £24.3 billion cumulated over five years.
kpis.signal: Stable investment at £4.9 billion, reflecting continued fibre deployment.

kpis.name: Normalized free cash flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after capital investments and adjustments.
kpis.description: Normalized free cash flow improved significantly to £1.6 billion in FY25, compared to £1.3 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Significant cash flow improvement (+23%), demonstrating progress toward £2bn targets in FY27 and £3bn in FY30.

kpis.name: Number of mobile sites
kpis.explanation: Total number of mobile sites operated by BT.
kpis.description: BT operates approximately 19,500 mobile sites across the UK.
kpis.signal: Extensive mobile network across approximately 19,500 sites.

kpis.name: Operating cash flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated by operating activities before capital investments.
kpis.description: Operating cash flow reached £7.0 billion in FY25, up 17% compared to £6.0 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Strong improvement in operating cash generation.

kpis.name: Profit before tax
kpis.description: Profit before tax stood at £1.3 billion in FY25, up 8% compared to £1.2 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Improved net profitability despite revenue decline.

kpis.name: Basic EPS
kpis.description: EPS reached 10.8 pence in FY25, up 24% compared to 8.7 pence in FY24.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.explanation: Dividend paid to shareholders per ordinary share.
kpis.description: Dividend per share stood at 8.16 pence for FY25, reflecting BT's commitment to delivering value to shareholders while continuing to invest in future growth.
kpis.signal: Progressive dividend policy maintained with a 2% increase for FY25.

kpis.name: Group Net Promoter Score
kpis.explanation: Customer satisfaction and loyalty indicator measured by Net Promoter Score.
kpis.description: Group NPS improved from 24.8 in FY24 to 29.5 in FY25, reflecting efforts to place customers at the center of decision-making.
kpis.signal: Substantial improvement in customer satisfaction following focus on customer experience.

kpis.name: Employee engagement
kpis.explanation: Percentage of employees feeling engaged and empowered to make decisions and innovate.
kpis.description: 82% of employees feel positive about developing new ways to serve customers and are empowered to make decisions, according to the 'Your Say' survey. This score exceeds the UK benchmark by 8%.
kpis.signal: Very high engagement level, 8% above UK benchmark.

kpis.name: UK economic contribution
kpis.explanation: BT Group's total economic contribution to the British economy.
kpis.description: BT Group added over £22.8 billion to the British economy, connecting people, businesses, and society.
kpis.signal: Major economic impact on the UK.

risks.title: Dependency on Ofcom regulation and regulatory uncertainty
risks.score_rationale: Risk highlighted in CEO and Chairman letter (pages 3-4, 7). Intensive language: key priority, long-term certainty and predictability. Stable trend but critical: Ofcom Telecoms Access Review launched in FY25 determines future investment returns. Category weight very high: sector regulation determines viability of BT's business model.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and rising digital threats
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly raised by CEO (page 7): digital safety, stopping two million potential cyber-attacks every day, quantum technologies. Intensive language: 24/7 threats, increasingly sophisticated. Upward trend: mention of cutting-edge technologies (quantum) signals escalating threats. Category weight critical for critical infrastructure operator.

risks.title: Intense competition in fixed and mobile connectivity
risks.score_rationale: Risk implicit but major: CEO mentions return to growth and stabilize our consumer base (page 7), indicating competitive pressures. Moderate language but clear context: historical customer losses over three years before stabilization. Stable trend but structural. Category weight high: UK market saturated with Virgin Media, Sky, Vodafone.

risks.title: Operational complexity and transformation execution risks
risks.score_rationale: Major risk raised by CEO (pages 5-8): radically simplify and digitalize, migration of 1.2m customers from legacy PSTN network, reduction from 300 to 30 sites. Intensive language: scale of BT's modernization agenda, essential we have the right management team. Upward trend: accelerated transformation underway. Category weight high: five-year execution risk.

risks.title: Dependency on massive infrastructure fibre investments
risks.score_rationale: Structural risk: CEO emphasizes largest investor in UK infrastructure (page 7), capex £4.9bn annually, target 30m premises with full fibre by 2030. Intensive language: sustained peak levels of investment. Upward trend: 20% build rate increase in FY26. Category weight high: capex intensive, long-term returns.

risks.title: Dependency on technology suppliers and key partners
risks.score_rationale: Implicit risk: CEO mentions partnerships with the world's best technology providers (page 7) and Global Fabric (world-first platform). Moderate language but clear dependency. Stable trend. Category weight moderate: BT depends on suppliers for innovation (Wi-Fi 7, 5G, quantum).

risks.title: Risks related to critical services and social responsibility
risks.score_rationale: Emerging risk: CEO emphasizes custodians of some of the country's most iconic brands and digital inclusion (pages 7-8). Moderate language but growing responsibility. Upward trend: increased engagement on digital inclusion, child safety. Category weight moderate: reputational and regulatory risk.

risks.title: Risk of asset impairment and future depreciation
risks.score_rationale: Implicit risk: massive legacy PSTN migration (1.2m customers) and product simplification suggest depreciation of legacy assets. Moderate language but clear context. Upward trend: accelerated legacy migration. Category weight moderate: accounting and balance sheet risk.

ai_positioning.summary: BT does not appear as a leader in generative AI. Its positioning focuses on network infrastructure (fibre, 5G) and connectivity as the foundation of the digital economy, with no direct mention of AI products or services in the 2025 annual report.
evidence: No mention of generative AI or AI APIs in the provided report excerpt.
Primary focus on connectivity, full fibre, and 5G as growth drivers and transformation enablers.
No references to AI partnerships or AI offerings for enterprise or consumer segments in the analyzed sections.
Report emphasizes operational transformation, customer experience, and physical infrastructure.
